title: Ahead of the lectures: reconstruction and the DFT (Midterm 2)
text:
Every question generates a new random variant each time you ask for one. A question is worth 6 points: 2 for the first correct variant, and more for consecutive correct variants. You get 3 tries per variant; after a submission a second hint unlocks and the full worked solution is shown once you have used your tries or answered correctly.

Ahead of the lectures. These topics are taught after Lecture 17 and carry most of the points on past Midterm 2 exams: ideal D/A reconstruction, digital filtering of analog signals (A/D → Hd → D/A), the DFT and its properties, zero padding, DFT spectral analysis and circular convolution. The questions follow the notation of the recent Midterm 2 keys and the 2019 course notes; come back to them as the lectures arrive.
